question: What asset authorization flags can a Stellar issuer set on a regulated token, and what does each one do?

golden.answer: An issuer can set four flags. AUTH_REQUIRED: the issuer must approve a trustline before it can hold the asset. AUTH_REVOCABLE: the issuer can revoke or freeze a trustline's authorization. AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED: the issuer can claw back from trustlines created afterward; it requires AUTH_REVOCABLE. AUTH_IMMUTABLE: locks the flags permanently.
keyFacts: AUTH_REQUIRED means the issuer must approve a trustline before it can hold the asset.
AUTH_REVOCABLE lets the issuer revoke or freeze a trustline's authorization.
AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED allows burning from new trustlines and requires AUTH_REVOCABLE.
AUTH_IMMUTABLE locks the authorization flags against any further change.
avoid: Do NOT invent flags such as AUTH_FROZEN or AUTH_KYC_REQUIRED.
Do NOT claim flags can change after AUTH_IMMUTABLE, or that clawback works without AUTH_REVOCABLE.
golden.notes: Hex values and the managing operations (set_options, set_trust_line_flags) are optional extras.

sources.note: Golden audit 2026-11-02 verifier: "With the `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set, any *subsequent* trustlines established with this account will have clawbacks enabled. ... Note that this flag requires that revocable is also set."

Golden audit 2026-11-02 verifier: "This causes every subsequent trustline established to any assets issued by that account to have the `TRUSTLINE_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` set automatically. ... You can only clear a flag, not set it. So clearing a clawback flag on a trustline is irreversible."

Golden audit 2026-11-02 verifier: "In order to execute a clawback of an amount in an account, an issuer account must have its `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set when the account holding the asset created its trustline. ... `TRUSTLINE_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG`, that is set at the time the trustline is created if the issuer account of the asset of the trustline has its `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set."
Golden audit 2026-11-02 verifier: "With the AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG flag set, any subsequent trustlines established with this account will have clawbacks enabled."

Golden audit 2026-11-02 verifier: "Setting `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED` does not make previously established trustlines clawback-enabled. The issuer can claw back from a trustline only if that trustline has `TRUSTLINE_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG`"

evidence: Live A 2026-11-14: https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/control-asset-access -- 'Note that this flag requires that revocable is also set.'

corroboration.claim: AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED lets the issuer burn balances on trustlines created after it is set.

evidence.note: Exact quote: "With the `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set, any *subsequent* trustlines established with this account will have clawbacks enabled."
Exact quote: "an issuer account must have its `AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED_FLAG` flag set when the account holding the asset created its trustline."

corroboration.claim: AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED requires AUTH_REVOCABLE; four flags exist.

evidence.note: Note that this flag requires that revocable is also set.

truth.notes:
Canonical, verified vs control-asset-access docs. Four flags: AUTH_REQUIRED(0x1), AUTH_REVOCABLE(0x2), AUTH_IMMUTABLE(0x4), AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED(0x8). Docs confirm clawback flag 'requires that revocable is also set'. Trap: hallucinated flag names; missing the AUTH_REVOCABLE precondition.
Also good if the answer: AUTH_REVOCABLE must be enabled before AUTH_CLAWBACK_ENABLED can be set. | Flags are managed via Set Options / Set Trustline Flags operations.
Golden cites: developers.stellar.org control-asset-access / clawbacks docs.
